chunks: There is no one who raises the talbiyah except that whatever is to his right, from any thing up to the furthest reach of the earth, and whatever is to his left up to the furthest reach of the earth, also raises it; and the two angels say to him: 'Rejoice, O servant of Allah,' and Allah gives glad tidings to no servant except of Paradise.

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةِ: the ritual proclamation of Labbayka in pilgrimage
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, the final good news mentioned in the hadith
key_terms.الْمَلَكَانِ: the two angels who give glad tidings
key_terms.مَقْطَعِ التُّرَابِ: the furthest limit or end of the earth
key_terms.مُهِلٍّ: one who raises the talbiyah for hajj or 'umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of reciting the talbiyah during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the immense spiritual resonance of the talbiyah during hajj, portraying creation on both sides of the pilgrim as joining in this response. It also presents the talbiyah as a cause of divine glad tidings, with the angels announcing good news that culminates in Paradise.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2140 - Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:

"There is no one who raises their voice in Talbiyah (Labbaik Allahumma Labbaik) except that everything to their right up to the ends of the earth and everything to their left up to the ends of the earth also proclaims the Talbiyah. Then the two angels say to them: 'Rejoice, O servant of Allah (swt)!' And Allah (swt) does not give glad tidings to a servant except with Paradise."
